A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Few-Shot Detector (FSD) study. All 11 pages of v1 and 12 pages of v2 are readable, including equations, figures, tables and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original FSD experiments on GenImage, including detection accuracies, cross-generator classification results, feature visualizations and shot-count ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains the original FSD experiments, including Tables 1–2 and the feature-space and shot-count analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes the loss accumulation from adding log-softmax to subtracting it, aligning the written algorithm with the negative-log-probability objective already stated in v1. The architecture, prototype computation and inference procedures remain unchanged; this correction does not establish an implementation change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same GenImage data, generator groups, merged Stable Diffusion category and zero-shot/few-shot detection tasks. SDXL, DiT and FLUX appear in v2's new conceptual Figure 1, without corresponding evaluations.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains CNNSpot, Spec, F3Net, GramNet, DIRE and LARE2. The binary ResNet-50 comparator in the multi-class ablation is also retained. Changed baseline scores do not alter comparator membership.

E3.justification: FSD's stated splits, preprocessing, metrics and training settings are unchanged. Section 4.3 now specifies averaging five baseline classifiers trained on non-test categories, whereas v1 describes cross-subset averaging without that exact pool. The accompanying score revisions leave unclear whether aggregation changed or its description was clarified.

E4.justification: The cross-generator analysis, six-classifier t-SNE visualizations, 1–200-shot sensitivity study and FSD-versus-binary-classifier analysis are retained. Their questions and evidence are unchanged; the new introductory figure is explanatory rather than experimental.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or error bars. Averaging classifiers trained on different categories is not new uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces all six baseline result rows: for example, LARE2's average accuracy changes from 76.7% to 72.5%, and DIRE's from 65.0% to 58.7%. FSD's zero-shot/10-shot averages remain 77.1%/84.1%, and all Table 2 results are identical. The headline margin therefore rises from 7.4 to 11.6 percentage points through revised comparator values.

T1.justification: The sign correction in Algorithm 1 fixes the mathematical inconsistency between its loss expression and the stated negative-log-likelihood minimization objective. The prototype and classification equations otherwise remain equivalent; no new theoretical results or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction strengthen the quantified advantage over prior methods from 7.4 to 11.6 percentage points. The central claims about few-shot reformulation, generator-specific categories and generalization without further training remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the explanations for VQDM difficulty, unseen-class clustering and the benefit of generator-specific categories. Limitations concerning unavailable support samples and substantially different generators are also retained; wording refinements add no substantive interpretation.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link in the abstract and explicitly documents the five non-test-category classifiers used for baseline averaging. The existing architecture, hyperparameters, preprocessing and A100 hardware disclosures remain unchanged. Repository contents are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: The bibliography adds Kukanov et al. on speech-deepfake meta-learning, Sha et al.'s DE-FAKE and Wolleb et al. on medical anomaly detection. Section 2.2 also changes Chen et al.'s description from using a few patches to a single patch. Overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 extensively edits sentences and paragraphs across the abstract, introduction, related work and method, with further language refinements throughout the experiments and conclusion. Grammar, terminology and task explanations are revised broadly, although the main section sequence is preserved.

P2.justification: V2 adds an introductory conceptual figure and substantially redraws the detection pipeline and prototype illustrations. It also enlarges and restyles the shot-count plot and relocates the binary-comparison figure. Existing t-SNE panels are retained, and the principal table structures remain stable.

improvement.justification: V2 improves clarity through extensive prose editing and redesigned explanatory figures, corrects Algorithm 1's loss sign, and adds code-access and baseline-averaging information. These are useful but limited gains: experimental coverage and FSD results remain unchanged, while the revised comparator values driving the larger headline margin are not fully explained.
